durability.recordLayout: One project/main contract; separate item and job records. Do not paste the whole ledger into a new context.
newContextReadOrder: actual editor/project and live job readback
writeBoundaries: Before every external mutation: commit prepared intent/fingerprint/target
After submission: commit original handle and tool evidence
After each item/batch, before context compaction, handoff or stopping: persist save version, evidence, next work, budget and decisions
jobRules: prepared may already have caused a remote write if interrupted before recording the handle
Observation timeout or missing handle does not prove failure
Inspect original handle/target and prove terminal before a conflicting retry
Do not reopen terminal jobs; new retry references retryOf
After two failures of one fingerprint/strategy, change method with evidence
Terminal attempt snapshots and strategy are immutable; attach later evidence to the item/project record
inputSnapshot, expectedChange and baseline are immutable from prepared; changed source needs a separately identified linked attempt after resolving any conflicting live job
durability.validationBoundary: The helper validates records and transactions; Agent must inspect real evidence, complete full-map acceptance and execute the next work. It does not call tools, schedule turns or create a background service.
scopeRules: scope.exclude contains stable item IDs, not free-form region names
Items default to in-scope. Keep excluded historical records instead of deleting them.
First update project scope.exclude with the user-requested ID; then set item.scopeMembership=excluded with scopeChange requestedBy=user, nonempty reason and evidence.
Completion compares map.itemIds against current in-scope items; excluded history remains listable, and unresolved jobs still block completion.
To restore: reopen a completed project as active, reactivate the retained item, then remove its ID from project scope.exclude and re-review map coverage.
